title: Bag-of-Words, n-grams & TF-IDF
interviewAnswer: Bag-of-words represents term counts while n-grams add local order; TF-IDF downweights ubiquitous terms. These sparse representations remain strong, interpretable baselines for many text classification/search problems.
keyPoints: Linear models pair well with sparse features.
why: Bag-of-Words, n-grams & TF-IDF appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Bag-of-words represents term counts while n-grams add local order; TF-IDF downweights ubiquitous terms. These sparse representations remain strong, interpretable baselines for many text classification/search problems. Vocabulary can be huge/sparse. Linear models pair well with sparse features. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Classify support tickets with TF-IDF bigrams + logistic regression before fine-tuning a transformer.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.

production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
